introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Tume and your address GHS Nyakom.* ***The usual introduction to the letter must not be more than 20 words.***

*Use of a different name and /or address will be seriously penalised. This holds true for details that can help reveal your true identity, school and/or family.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for what happened last year, with the imparfait for habits before the purchase and the présent for the situation today. Format: informal letter (place and date, salutation, introduction of no more than 20 words, body, closing, signature), with the imposed name Tume and address GHS Nyakom. The friend's first name (Paul) is invented for the salutation; the topic does not impose one.

**Model essay** (143, or 148 if elisions are counted as two words words)

GHS Nyakom, le 10 juin 2025

Cher Paul,

J'espère que tu vas bien. Je t'écris pour te raconter une belle nouvelle.

L'an passé, à l'occasion de leur anniversaire de mariage, papa a acheté à maman un écran plasma. Il l'a rapporté un samedi soir, après avoir économisé pendant des mois. Nous avons tous été vraiment surpris en le voyant arriver avec ce grand carton.

Les réactions ont été très joyeuses. Maman a longuement embrassé papa et les petits ont sauté de joie. Mon grand frère, lui, a aussitôt voulu regarder un match de football.

Cet écran a vraiment amélioré notre vie en famille. Autrefois, chacun restait seul dans sa chambre. Maintenant, nous nous réunissons chaque soir au salon pour regarder un film ou les informations, puis nous discutons ensemble. Nous nous disputons moins et nous rions beaucoup plus.

Viens vite nous voir un jour pour en profiter avec nous.

Ton ami,
Tume

**Notes**

The introduction ("J'espère que tu vas bien. Je t'écris pour te raconter une belle nouvelle.") has 13 words (15 if the elisions are counted as two words), so it respects the limit of 20. The letter covers the three bullet points: the circumstances (wedding anniversary, a Saturday evening), the reactions (mother, young children, elder brother) and the improvement of family life (the family gathers in the living room). The word count runs from the introduction to the closing formula; the address line, the date, the friend's first name and the signature are not counted.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Using a different name or address, or details that reveal the real identity of the candidate: this is seriously penalised.
2. Writing an introduction of more than 20 words, or forgetting the letter format (place, date, salutation, closing formula).
